description:
First end-to-end QA pass of the Results Explorer (run on Chromium 147 and
Firefox 148 against the dev server at http://localhost:5173/results/) found
four real product bugs, plus one open question about a possibly-removed UI
control. This item tracks the investigation and remediation of each.

Source: QA tester report on commit ca9a8ed9b, scored against the test plan
written by the agent. Filtered out test-plan errors (the SSB route mistake)
and known-upstream warnings (DuckDB-WASM exception-handling, JSX-source
babel plugin warning, Chrome-headless cold-load latency tracked separately
as `enable-duckdb-wasm-http-range-reads-for-registered-urls`).

Bugs to fix:
  B1  PlatformIndex tables have static <th> headers — no sort handlers.
  B2  /results/p/duckdb/ and /results/p/polars/ render empty even though
      the DuckDB browser store has 4 + 2 rows for those platforms.
  B3  /results/does-not-exist/ renders an empty BenchmarkIndex instead of
      the NotFound page (preact-router ":benchmark/" matches anything).
  B4  TimeSeries on platform pages emits a Preact duplicate-key warning
      when multiple results share a run_date.

Open question (resolve before any UI change):
  Q1  ResultDetail and Compare both have `primaryMetric` state read from
      `?metric=` URL param, but no in-page toggle UI. Is this an
      intentional URL-only contract or a regression?

work_units.notes:
DECISION: B2 is real and intermittent. The casing/projection bug
and the equality-mismatch bug are both ruled out. The mechanism
that produces the intermittency is NOT YET PINNED — w3 must
instrument before implementing a fix.

Evidence (what we know):
  - Direct DuckDB inspection: `platform_index_rows` for the
    production corpus contains clean ASCII slugs ('duckdb',
    'polars', 'datafusion', 'sqlite') with no whitespace, casing,
    or NULL oddities. → rules out the projection/casing class.
  - PlatformIndex.tsx:48 filter is `r.platform_id === platform`
    (strict-equality ASCII strings). The same code path renders
    the same data shape for every platform; if it failed for
    "polars" it would also fail for "sqlite". → rules out the
    equality-mismatch class.
  - Three serial invocations of the original manual repro produced
    P/F, F/F, P/P with the warm run finishing in 1-3s — strong
    intermittency signal correlated with WASM warmth.

Mechanism (NOT confirmed — three plausible candidates):
  1. DuckDB-WASM cold-load partial data: a SELECT resolves
     before the runtime has fetched all of the table's pages.
     Underlying range-read issue tracked as
     `enable-duckdb-wasm-http-range-reads-for-registered-urls`
     (see results-explorer/src/db.ts:67-77).
  2. Preact useEffect cleanup race: PlatformIndex.tsx:24-40
     uses `let cancelled = false; if (!cancelled) setRows(r)`.
     A fast navigation between platform pages could drop the
     setRows call.
  3. Shared `initPromise` race in db.ts:48-96: `getDb()` reuses
     `initPromise` across mounts; component-ordering quirks
     could leave the cached `dbInstance` in an inconsistent
     state.

None of the three has direct evidence yet. Picking a fix without
instrumentation risks fixing the wrong layer.

The manual overlay repro was replaced in w3 by the route-backed
regression guard at
`results-explorer/e2e/failures/platform-index-cold-load.spec.ts`.
work_units.summary: Investigate B2 — root-cause empty PlatformIndex for duckdb/polars

work_units.notes:
DECISION: No toggle should exist. The original Q1 framing was
based on an incomplete read of the code; the actual contract is
stronger than "URL-only" — it is "benchmark-derived, not
user-configurable."

Evidence:
  - `git log -G"primaryMetric"` returns ONE commit ever
    touching the symbol in pages/ — f9d08d38b, the migration
    that originally populated develop. There is no removed
    button in history.
  - ResultDetail.tsx:64-66 calls
    `getPrimaryMetricForBenchmark(data.benchmark)` and feeds
    the result into `setPrimaryMetric`. Compare.tsx:82-84 does
    the same with `details[0]!.benchmark`. The setter is NEVER
    fired from a user-driven event in either file.
  - The metric is therefore determined by the benchmark family's
    ranking config (e.g. ClickBench → power_score, TPC-H →
    display_geomean_ms). Letting users override it via a toggle
    would produce incorrect cross-benchmark comparisons.
  - Cross-benchmark comparisons are foreclosed by Compare.tsx:64-71,
    which rejects mixed-benchmark sets with "Cannot compare results
    from different benchmarks: ...". Since every Compare and
    ResultDetail view is single-benchmark, the per-benchmark metric
    is unambiguous — a toggle would only enable wrong metric choices,
    not legitimate ones.

Implication for w7:
  - Drop §4.2 ("Primary metric toggle (power_score ↔
    display_geomean_ms) updates the chart") from the test plan.
  - Drop §5.3 (same expectation in Compare).
  - Optionally add a positive assertion that confirms the
    benchmark-derived contract — but capture the actual axis-label
    text emitted by chartRegistry.ts:233-240 for each benchmark's
    primary_metric (run the relevant pages once and copy the
    rendered label). Do NOT guess the text; the labels are
    generated, not hard-coded.

No follow-up TODO needed; the feature should not be added.
work_units.summary: Resolve Q1 — confirm whether ResultDetail/Compare primary-metric toggle should exist

work_units.notes:
Copied the button-in-th pattern from ResultDetail.tsx:326-352
and applied to all five sortable columns in PlatformIndex.tsx
(Benchmark, Scale, Date, Power Score, Geomean). Geomean was
added beyond the original four to keep the UX consistent —
otherwise the user would see four sort arrows and a stuck
Geomean column.

Initial sort state is `{ key: "geomean_ms", direction: "asc" }`,
preserving the prior default (fastest first, nulls last) per
the must_preserve guard. The new sort comparator routes string
columns through localeCompare and numeric columns through `av - bv`,
with nulls always last regardless of direction.

New tests in src/pages/__tests__/PlatformIndex.test.tsx cover:
  - default sort = geomean_ms asc, nulls last
  - Geomean click → direction flip (asc → desc, nulls still last)
  - Benchmark click → alphabetical asc, stable sort within ties
  - Power Score click → nulls last in both directions

Scope note: the original B1 listed four columns (Benchmark, Scale,
Date, Power Score). w4 deliberately extended click-sort to Geomean
as well — leaving four sortable headers next to a static fifth
adjacent numeric column would have looked like a bug rather than
a constraint. Default state is unchanged so the must_preserve
guard still holds.

Post-review (W4 review): added aria-sort="ascending|descending|none"
to each sortable <th>; added an sr-only direction announcement
inside the active button so screen readers communicate state on
sort change. Replaced localeCompare on run_date with strict
lexicographic compare (ISO 8601 makes this chronologically
correct without dragging in locale collation). Documented the
"nulls last in both directions" choice in code. Tests now resolve
row order via data-testid on PlatformRow's <tr>, not via parsing
aria-label substrings; added a keyboard-activation test (focus +
keyDown Enter + click) and an aria-sort assertion test.

Verification: 285/285 vitest passes, tsc clean.

work_units.notes:
Implemented approach (a): inside BenchmarkIndex.tsx, after
results finish loading and before the title is rendered, check
whether `benchmarkResults.length === 0` (no row in the loaded
set whose `benchmark` matches the URL slug). Approach (b) —
maintaining a known-benchmarks set from cohort_metadata — was
rejected because `results` already carries the answer; threading
a second source of truth would invite drift.

Post-review (W5 review): the original guard conflated "unknown
slug" with "known slug, no data yet." The published corpus has
data for 2 of the 8 entries in BENCHMARK_LABELS (src/utils.ts);
the other 6 (tpcds, clickbench, nyctaxi, h2odb, datavault, plus
ssb-as-alias) all 404'd, suggesting they were unsupported. Now
a 3-state guard:
  - Unknown slug (not in BENCHMARK_LABELS) →
    <NotFound message="Benchmark X is not part of the published corpus." />
  - Known benchmark with no rows → an inline empty-corpus state
    ("No published results yet for ClickBench. The benchmark is
    supported by BenchBox but no runs have been ingested into
    the public corpus.").
  - Known benchmark with rows → the existing BenchmarkIndex flow.

Supporting changes:
  - utils.ts: BENCHMARK_LABELS exported; new helper
    isKnownBenchmark(slug) returns slug in BENCHMARK_LABELS.
  - NotFound: gained an optional `message` prop so callers can
    give the user a more specific 404 reason than the default
    "Page not found.".

Comment near the guard documents an incidental safety property:
the summary-fetch useEffect is safe for both empty cases because
its `phases.length === 0` early-return catches them. A future
decoupling of `phases` from `benchmarkResults` would need to add
its own early-return.

e2e coverage: three specs in routes/not-found.spec.ts —
  - 3-segment unknown path → preact-router default → 404.
  - Unknown :benchmark slug → 404 with benchmark-specific message.
  - Known benchmark (clickbench) with no rows → empty-corpus
    heading, NOT a 404.

Verification: 285/285 vitest pass; tsc clean; 3/3 chromium e2e
pass.
work_units.summary: Fix B3 — route unknown-benchmark slugs to NotFound

work_units.notes:
Root cause: TimeSeries.tsx:173 used `key={p.date}` for each
<circle>, but two runs of the same platform on the same date
produced two points with the same `date`. Preact's reconciliation
then emitted "Each child in a list should have a unique key prop."

Fix: thread `result_id` from the source ChartHistoricalEntry into
the SeriesPoint shape, then key the circle on `p.resultId`.
result_id is guaranteed unique per result (it's the canonical ID
assigned by ExplorerPipeline) so no composite is needed.

New unit test in charts.smoke.test.tsx asserts:
  - Three runs (two sharing a date) render three circles.
  - No duplicate-key warning is emitted on console.warn or
    console.error.

Verification: 286/286 vitest pass; tsc clean.

Post-review (W6 review): four findings applied.

R1 — replaced the spy-on-console regression assertion with a
structural one. <circle> elements now carry data-result-id; the
test queries them and asserts new Set(ids).size === ids.length.
Independent of Preact's dev-mode warning channel and survives
production tree-shaking.

C1 — swept analogous patterns. PercentileLadder.tsx:107 used
key={row.platform} which would collide if two rows have the
same platform name (e.g. DuckDB tuned + DuckDB notuning).
Added result_id to PercentileStatsRow, threaded through from
ChartPanel's caller (summary.platforms.flatMap), and keyed on
it. New unit test covers the variant-tuning case explicitly.
DivergingBarChart.tsx:141 used key={entry.platform} on the
inner bar map; switched to composite `${entry.platform}-${si}`
since the entry shape there doesn't carry result_id.

N1 — TimeSeries now dedupes its `entries` prop on result_id
before any further processing. Defensive against caller bugs
that double-count results (e.g. JOIN regressions in upstream
queries). New test asserts only 2 circles render when 3 entries
with 2 sharing a result_id are passed.

N2 — comment near the new TimeSeries test explains: the
structural ID-uniqueness check is the true regression guard;
future contributors should not delete it without an equivalent
replacement.

Verification: 288/288 vitest pass; tsc clean.
